name: RIKEN and Fujitsu K computer
description: RIKEN and Fujitsu's research supercomputer in Kobe connected SPARC64 VIIIfx nodes with the original six-dimensional Tofu interconnect. The system reached 10.51 PFlop/s in LINPACK before entering shared use.

date.basis: June TOP500 results date the documented demonstration.

events.statement: The June 2011 TOP500 listing reported a measured LINPACK result of 8,162 TFlop/s for the K computer.

evidence.supports: The listing identifies K and reports 8,162.00 TFlop/s Rmax.
Identifies the installation at AICS in Kobe.

date.label: by 2011-11-02
date.basis: RIKEN and Fujitsu had announced the result by 2 November.

events.statement: With 88,128 CPUs, K achieved 10.51 PFlop/s in LINPACK while still under development.

evidence.supports: Joint announcement explicitly reports the measured 10.51 PFlop/s and the 88,128-CPU configuration.
The benchmark list reports 10,510.00 TFlop/s Rmax for that configuration.

date.basis: Start of shared use in the RIKEN job archive.

events.statement: The K computer entered shared research use at RIKEN in Kobe.

evidence.supports: Operator documents the day shared use started and records jobs by month.
RIKEN describes the researcher opening and Kobe site.

date.basis: Operator retrospectively dates completion of the service mission.

events.statement: The K computer concluded its seven-year service mission.
events.scope: End of the shared service mission.

evidence.supports: RIKEN confirms the service mission ended on 16 August and distinguishes eventual power-off and dismantling.

earliest_record.rationale: The June TOP500 entry is the earliest benchmark retained here for an operating K configuration. The design and installation predate it.

research.note: Participant, operator and benchmark records distinguish staged operation from the shared-use lifecycle.

places.note: System operated at RIKEN's AICS in Kobe.

measures.subject: K computer, 88,128 CPUs
measures.conditions: Published LINPACK run on the November configuration.

links.statement: The June 2011 K configuration used Fujitsu’s original Tofu to interconnect its compute nodes.
links.scope: The actual built K system and its node-to-node network.

evidence.supports: The system's original Tofu was developed for K and used a dedicated controller chip.
Identifies original Tofu as the interconnect in the benchmarked machine.

evidence.locator: §§5.1–5.2 and §6.2, topology-aware mapping and results on K
evidence.supports: Applications measured on K exploit the actual network dimensions and simultaneous communication.

links.statement: K’s compute nodes used Fujitsu’s SPARC64 VIIIfx for numerical work.
links.scope: The actual built K system and its processor configuration.

evidence.supports: Identifies the VIIIfx as the processor being developed for Fujitsu's petascale supercomputer.
Names SPARC64 VIIIfx in the benchmarked machine.
Hiroshima University researchers used its double-precision SIMD in a solver port on the operating K computer.
